lines.say: This man is looking at his own son,
and searching for mercy.
This is Peter the Great Interrogating the Tsarevich Alexei,
painted by Nikolai Ge in 1871.
Most people see an emperor questioning his son,
accused of plotting to seize power.
Before the sentence,
Peter searches his son's eyes for remorse.
And the picture seems to agree.
The tsar sits still,
and the son lowers his head.
But look at the floor.
A paper lies dropped beside the table.
According to documents published by Alexander Herzen,
Alexei was strangled by order of Peter the Great.
Ge himself wrote that after studying the documents,
there could be no sympathy for Peter.
This isn't a father hoping for remorse.
It's a judge who has already decided.
So was Peter looking for remorse,
or only waiting to sign?
